items.headline: Chip stocks crater: Nvidia -9.3%, AMD -17.3%, Philadelphia Semiconductor Index down more than 12% in one session
items.why: The market is repricing how fast the AI data-center buildout can proceed now that rising electricity costs have made new data centers a political issue, which puts chip and data-center capex forecasts at risk.

items.headline: Microsoft reportedly scrutinizing Nscale, Nebius and IREN after construction delays and cost overruns; Nebius and IREN fall more than 13%
items.why: If the largest AI cloud buyer tightens oversight of third-party capacity providers, the financing and timelines behind rented AI compute become less certain.

items.headline: About 600,000 Nvidia H200 chips reportedly sit in Hong Kong while Beijing withholds large-scale mainland import approval (unconfirmed by Nvidia)
items.why: China demand for Nvidia's export-cleared chips is gated by Beijing's approvals, not just US licensing, so a large inventory can sit idle and weigh on expected China revenue.

items.headline: AMD discloses plans to buy World Labs (~$8.2B) and Taalas (~$2.9B) for about $11.1B combined, both subject to closing conditions
items.why: AMD is spending heavily on 3D world-model and inference-chip capability just as the market questions AI capex, a test of whether acquirers get rewarded for buying growth.

items.headline: Binance estimates a $6.3B security breach, the largest crypto hack on record; says it has covered about 90% of losses
items.why: A loss of this size at the largest exchange tests whether its reserve fund can absorb it without user losses, and it adds to risk-off pressure on crypto.

items.headline: FBI attributes the Binance theft to North Korea's TraderTraitor group; stolen assets are being converted mainly into Ether
items.why: Conversion into Ether and attempts to launder it can create selling and on-chain flow pressure, while attribution to a state actor raises the odds of freezes and enforcement actions.

items.headline: Democrats win both chambers of Congress in the US midterms; Treasuries rally, 10-year yield falls to about 4.93% and the dollar softens
items.why: Divided government lowers the odds of new fiscal stimulus and sets up a 2027 debt-limit fight, while the shift in policy expectations is already moving yields, defense stocks and clean-energy shares.

items.why: With a strong manufacturing report (ISM 55.5) and the 10-year near 4.9%, the policy path is still toward tightening, which caps upside for gold and long-duration tech.

items.why: Energy prices are the main swing factor for inflation, so any talks breakthrough or collapse moves rate expectations, eurozone inflation (near 4%) and equities.

items.why: Metals are recovering as oil and the dollar ease, but prices are still capped by hawkish Fed pricing, so the October losses have not been reversed.
